summary: Prewarm handshake abort on canary interrupted by probe spike splits session pins and triggers cascading fallback
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled canary rollout for redwood-3b-v2 we observed an aborted prewarm handshake caused by a sudden health-probe spike from the edge-prober. Impact: ~12% of ByteScale tenant sessions were routed to fallback variants for ~18 minutes, causing increased latency and inconsistent outputs for batch inference jobs. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, canary slice ~5% traffic, control plane snapshot version v2026.03.09. Observed behavior: 1) Orchestrator begins prewarm for canary instances. 2) Edge health-prober issues >50 fast consecutive probes for several hosts; probe responses include intermittent timeouts. 3) Prewarm handshake for affected cohort aborts mid-way; controller marks prewarm as failed and emits prewarm-abort event. 4) Session pins were partially applied before abort, producing split pin state across edge and orchestrator leading to repeated fallback routing and opaque session duplication.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy canary slice (5%) for redwood-3b-v2 to dedicated pool in us-east-1 with prewarm enabled
Simulate a burst of failed/slow health-check responses from the edge host (50+ probes within 60s)
Observe orchestrator logs for prewarm-handshake timeouts and prewarm-abort events
Send steady tenant traffic that exercises session affinity and observe routing decisions and model selection

comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10T09:18:00Z: Confirming customer impact — ByteScale reports intermittent high latency and degraded quality for scheduled batch runs. Currently throttling non-critical background jobs for the tenant.

Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-10T10:03:00Z: Temporary mitigation applied: forced pin-resync on the cohort and pinned sessions were reissued from control-plane snapshot v2026.03.09. Observed fallback counts decreased after resync. Still seeing sporadic edge-probe timeouts.

ByteScale (Customer) 2026-03-10T10:22:00Z: Thank you — we saw throughput recover but some outputs still reflected legacy-variant tokenization mismatches. We paused job queue and will hold new batches until cleared.

Lena Thompson (Eng) 2026-03-11T08:45:00Z: Hypothesis: prewarm handshake does not atomically commit pin metadata across orchestrator and edge shards; abort leaves partial state. We'll reproduce in staging with accelerated health probes.
investigation_notes: Initial correlation between prewarm-abort and spike in edge health-prober timeouts; edge prober configured to be aggressive for ded pool
Partial pin state recorded: control-plane shows commit for 3 shards while edge cache held different affinity tokens for same sessions
Router metrics show 1.5x fallback rate in cohort window 09:03-09:21 UTC; tokenization mismatch indicates some requests hit legacy variant
Related: SUP-412358 (stale-pin-consensus after region migrate delay) has similar partial commit symptoms; engineering linked for control-plane pin atomicity review
Repro in staging: able to trigger abort by dropping 60% of probe responses during prewarm window; observed same split pin state and fallback loop
next_steps: Engineering: add atomic two-phase commit for prewarm pin application across orchestrator + edge shard registries (PR drafted)
SRE: tune edge-prober backoff and add transient-probe-gating to prewarm path to avoid aborting on short spikes
Support: coordinate with ByteScale on rolling job resume schedule and confirm tokenization-consistency tests before full traffic promotion
Follow-up: postmortem and runbook update once fix merged and deployed
resolution: workaround applied: forced pin-resync and temporary prewarm gating reduced fallback rate; engineering to deliver atomic prewarm commit to prevent recurrence
